articles.title: Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games Held in Africa for First Time
articles.summary: The Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games were held in Senegal and marked a significant milestone in the Olympic calendar.
articles.content: The historic Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games took place in Africa for the first time, marking a significant milestone in the Olympic calendar. The city of Dakar, Senegal, proved to be an excellent host, showcasing its rich culture and warm hospitality to attendees from around the world. Manseen Logan, who was present at the event, described it as "beautiful" and an "entertaining clash of sports and culture." Commuting proved to be a significant logistical challenge during the Games, raising concerns about how future events would handle transportation issues. This problem has already been experienced by Logan in previous Olympic events, where getting around was often a daunting task. As someone who has attended several Olympic Games, including Tokyo 2020 and Paris 2024, Logan had high expectations for Dakar 2026. The event did not disappoint, with Senegal delivering a remarkable display of culture, athleticism, and young talent. Logan's organization, which serves as the official media partner for Team Liberia, allowed him to attend the Games in person, rather than remotely. This experience was invaluable, and Logan is now looking forward to sharing his insights about the event. Traveling between venues was a challenge, but not an insurmountable one, thanks to Dakar 2026's strategic planning and transportation arrangements. Complimentary buses and trains were available to carry participants from place to place, with the added convenience of an app that displayed bus schedules for easy navigation. However, my colleague and I encountered an issue when we had to pay for most of our train rides, despite being told by media accreditation volunteers that there were no more transport cards left. It turned out that this claim was incorrect, as we discovered later on, with the help of a volunteer at the train station who directed us to their boss, who had a stash of free train cards on his desk. The discrepancy between what we were told and what actually existed caused frustration, but it also highlighted the importance of effective communication in event planning. In the end, we managed to secure our transport cards, but not before experiencing some inconvenience that could have been avoided with better coordination. The Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games presented a unique fusion of cultures, seamlessly blending traditional African rhythms with modern sports. Entertainment during the break in the Taekwondo session was particularly noteworthy, featuring a talented lineup of Senegalese performers who brought the crowd to their feet. Both events I attended - taekwondo and breakdancing - were exceptional, showcasing incredible athleticism and artistry. The inclusion of entertainment added an extra layer of excitement, drawing the audience into the competitions. The breakdancing competition was a standout, with impressive displays of skill and creativity from young dancers who effortlessly spun on their heads and flipped through the air. Outside the breakdancing venue, African dancers performed to the infectious beat of Senegalese drummers, creating an electric atmosphere that drew in passersby. It was fascinating to watch as a volunteer joined in, breakdancing to the rhythm - a moment that highlighted the universal language of dance and music. The city's organizers made a conscious effort to involve Dakar's youth in every aspect of the Games, and it showed in the packed venues filled with students from local schools watching the matches. This was particularly heartwarming when elementary-school-aged athletes were seated alongside their schoolmates, all observing the action on the field or mat with wide eyes. The sheer number of young people involved in the event was staggering, with over 960,000 competition, ceremony, and Fan Zone tickets made available to kids, students, associations, and sports clubs. This approach not only gave the country's youngest citizens a chance to participate but also created an inspiring atmosphere that permeated every corner of the Games. The venues were filled with young people in their school uniforms, adding a lively and festive touch to the proceedings. The sheer number of volunteers was staggering - over 6,000 according to the Olympic website. However, not all were equally helpful in assisting visitors like myself. Some seemed more interested in socializing with friends than providing assistance. When I needed help, it often took me a while to find someone who was willing and able to assist me. This led me to develop a strategy for identifying volunteers who were likely to be more cooperative. I would look for the oldest volunteer present, as they often seemed more engaged in their duties. Transportation proved to be one of the most significant logistical challenges during my visit. Despite efforts to streamline the process, participants and spectators alike encountered difficulties navigating from venue to venue. The traffic congestion was notorious, with long delays common even on designated transportation routes. The experience left me pondering the upcoming LA 2028 Summer Olympic Games, which will take place in a city infamous for its gridlocked traffic. As someone who witnessed firsthand the challenges posed by inadequate transportation systems, I couldn't help but wonder if organizers are taking steps to mitigate these issues. The Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games showcased an impressive display of athleticism and talent among young breakdancers, leaving a lasting impression on those who witnessed their performances. The viral backlash that followed the introduction of breakdancing at the Paris 2024 Olympics may have been a valid reason to reconsider its inclusion in future games. However, the skills and energy demonstrated by these young dancers make a strong case for bringing back breakdancing as an Olympic sport. Their dedication and passion for the art form are undeniable, and their performances added a unique and captivating element to the games. The experience of covering Africa's first Youth Olympic Games was undoubtedly memorable, with the Dakar 2026 event being a resounding success in terms of showcasing local talent and culture. Overall, it was a pleasure to witness the excitement and energy that defined this historic event. articles.title: Caltech Students Revamp Mathathon Event to Embrace AI
articles.summary: Undergraduate students at Caltech reached a compromise with math community critics to revamp the competition's parameters and ensure controlled use of AI technology.
articles.content: Caltech students were facing a crisis when they met on a Friday in early September via video call. Their "mathathon event, designed to harness chatbots' power to tackle the world's most challenging math problems, was at risk of being canceled due to opposition from some members of the math community. The meeting brought about an unexpected turn of events as the undergraduate organizers reached a compromise with their critics. They agreed to revamp the competition's parameters in exchange for crucial support from the wider mathematical community. The deal marked a significant shift towards embracing AI while ensuring its use is controlled and measured. Ward, a Caltech student who was present at the meeting, initially advocated for the event's cancellation but later became involved in its organization. His involvement was instrumental in shaping the revised approach to AI in mathematics, paving the way for a more human-centered and controlled use of technology in the field. The changes implemented by the organizers reflect a growing recognition that AI can be a valuable tool in mathematics when used judiciously. The revamped mathathon event is now seen as a model for bridging deep-seated divisions within the math community, where some members advocate for a more cautious approach to AI while others see its potential benefits. The atmosphere was surprisingly convivial as students and faculty from Caltech's mathematics department gathered on campus. The event was a far cry from the heated debates that had been raging within the math community over the use of artificial intelligence in solving long-standing problems. Younger students who were enthusiastic about AI mingled with those who held more skeptical views, exchanging ideas in a spirit of mutual respect. Mathematicians and computer science enthusiasts alike roamed the picturesque campus, some pausing to pick up docile turtles or work on their laptops. The university's mathematics professor Sergei Gukov expressed his enthusiasm for this new era of collaboration. This unification is amazingly great, he said, highlighting the potential benefits of AI in mathematics. Mathematicians at every level had been grappling with the implications of OpenAI's breakthrough solution to the Navier-Stokes Millennium Prize question in September. The debate centered on whether mathematicians should harness AI and, if so, how they could use it responsibly. Some critics accused OpenAI of exploiting lists of open problems for self-promotion, disregarding the contributions of human researchers. The rapid advancement in artificial intelligence (AI) has sparked a heated debate among mathematicians over who should be credited for solving complex problems. The issue at hand is whether AI models or human researchers should take precedence in publishing solutions to renowned open problems. Leading figures in the math world are scrambling to develop their own AI models, an effort to regain control over AI-generated solutions that have been gaining prominence. However, this endeavor is taking place before these new models are fully developed, leaving many young mathematicians searching for alternative ways to stay relevant in a rapidly evolving field. In response to the changing landscape, some mathematicians are turning to closed and open-source models as a means of staying competitive. This shift is evident at the Caltech mathathon, where nearly every participant employed a combination of cutting-edge models that ran continuously in the background while they took brief breaks to recharge with energy drinks. The mathathon itself was initially designed to emulate the approach taken by big AI companies, which focus on tackling high-profile unsolved problems and publishing lengthy proofs, leaving human mathematicians to sift through them for useful information. The organizers of the mathathon took a crucial decision during a video call, agreeing to set aside open problems" that were initially at the center of controversy. Instead, participants would focus on finding innovative ways to tackle existing mathematical challenges. To make the event more inclusive and transparent, additional incentives were introduced for teams that could clearly explain their solutions, helping to sift through complex AI-generated data. This move was a response to concerns about the reliance on artificial intelligence in mathematics research. The organizers' efforts paid off as Anthropic agreed to end its sponsorship of $1 million in tokens, while OpenAI withdrew from the event due to mounting calls for its cancellation. Despite these challenges, the mathathon's creators remain hopeful that it will achieve its aspirations and redefine the role of human mathematicians in AI-driven research. He also highlighted Ukraine's efforts to develop its own military capabilities. The use of Ukrainian-made drones in this operation marks a significant development in Kyiv's long-range assault capabilities. The latest strike by Ukrainian forces has dealt a significant blow to Russia's naval presence in eastern Libya. According to two Libyan officials, the Russian navy corvette at the Benghazi Naval Base suffered severe damage from the attack. The base is located in the volatile region of eastern Libya. The aftermath of the strike was marked by loud explosions and visible fire at the base early on Sunday morning, as witnessed by residents in Benghazi. This incident comes amidst a long-standing division within Libya since the NATO-backed uprising toppled Muammar Qaddafi's regime in 2011. The country is currently governed by two rival administrations: one supported government based in Tripoli and another administration located in the east. Ukrainian forces have been operating in western Libya under a covert agreement with the West, utilizing the North African country's territory to launch strikes against Russian targets. In March, Ukrainian forces used Libyan territory to target a Russian tanker in the Mediterranean, according to Libyan officials. The Ukrainian security services claimed that two Russian ships, a cargo ship and a multipurpose corvette, were targeted in an attack off the coast of Libya. The cargo ship, MV Angara, was allegedly used to transport Russian military equipment and was often escorted by the corvette Merkury. According to the SBU, drones were launched from a "mothership" near the target location, with Russian defenses attempting to intercept them via air, sea, and land. articles.title: Renting Out Clothes Online Proves Lucrative for Former Wall Street Trader
articles.summary: A former Wall Street trader has turned to renting out her clothes online as a way to supplement her income as a private chef.
articles.content: A former Wall Street trader has turned to renting out her clothes online to supplement her income as a private chef. Wen Song's decision to leave finance was motivated by burnout after seven years in the industry. She had previously interviewed with fashion companies, but chose a hedge fund instead. Song's entrepreneurial venture began when she read an article about people making money by renting out their clothing. Her own collection of dresses sparked the idea to try it herself. With no prior experience, she put up a few items on Pickle and received a rental inquiry for one of her dresses right away. The item in question was a distinctive Gatsby-style fringe dress with sequins. The process of listing and renting out clothes on Pickle proved to be straightforward for Song. She found the app user-friendly and appreciated its ease of use. However, she did encounter some initial challenges related to shipping and customer service. These difficulties took several months to overcome before her rentals started to increase in volume. Song's experience with Pickle eventually led to her becoming a Star Lender on the platform. This status indicates a high level of success among renters. As her earnings grew, so did her flexibility in terms of work arrangements. Song's decision to leave finance was motivated by a desire for more autonomy and a better work-life balance. The rentals have also given Song an opportunity to declutter her closet while earning extra money each month. Her income from renting out clothes now totals $5,000 per month. Pricing my items competitively is crucial in generating volume on Pickle, especially for customers outside Boston who have to pay for shipping. To offset this additional cost, I typically price my items 20% to 30% lower than similar ones in major cities. This approach has allowed me to maintain a large inventory of around 460 items listed on the platform. As my business grew, I began investing in more pieces, initially focusing on items that I wore myself but now also purchasing multiples of my most successful designs. articles.summary: The Democratic National Committee has unveiled its plans for the 2028 presidential debates, setting out a detailed framework for what promises to be a crowded and competitive campaign season.
articles.content: The Democratic National Committee has unveiled its plans for the 2028 presidential debates, setting out a detailed framework for what promises to be a crowded and competitive campaign season. The party's rules will mirror those of the last open primary in 2020, with a focus on ensuring that candidates meet certain criteria before taking the stage. The debates themselves will be split into two nights each, with no more than 20 candidates qualifying overall - a clear acknowledgment of the large number of Democrats who are currently considering a run for the White House. The party has not yet announced specific dates or media partners for the first two debates, but this information is expected to be released in January. To qualify for the debate stage, candidates will need to meet certain criteria, including polling and grassroots fundraising figures. This approach aims to ensure that only viable and committed candidates make it onto the stage, rather than those who are simply seeking attention. The party's decision to require presidential candidates to sign a pledge denouncing "dark money spending in our primary" has been seen as a significant move. While this pledge does not have any real-world teeth, it is intended to attach a political cost to such outside spending and unite Democratic candidates behind the party's frustration with rampant outside influence. The exact details of how the pledge will be enforced are still unclear, but the move is being hailed as a key step in reducing the impact of dark money on the primary campaign. With so many Democrats already mulling over a run for the White House, this debate season promises to be one of the most competitive and closely watched in recent history. The Democratic National Committee has introduced new rules for its 2028 presidential debates, requiring candidates to adhere to a strict set of guidelines in order to participate. Among these requirements is the need for candidates to follow the party's newly established nominating calendar. Failure to do so may result in severe penalties, including the loss of delegates won in early-nominating states. The DNC has made it more difficult than before for candidates to undo this punishment. The Debate Planning Committee will be led by Minyon Moore and Roger Lau, with a team comprising experienced party strategists and campaign staff from past presidential campaigns. This includes individuals who worked on the campaigns of notable Democrats such as Kamala Harris, Joe Biden, Bernie Sanders, Elizabeth Warren, Amy Klobuchar, Hillary Clinton, and Barack Obama. The DNC's decision to start its debate calendar in June is seen as a strategic move to maintain momentum following the party's midterms victories. This approach mirrors the 2020 schedule, which saw the first debates take place in Miami with NBC News, MSNBC, and Telemundo hosting. Those events sparked intense clashes among Democratic hopefuls, with two 10-person debates held on consecutive days. The Democratic National Committee has outlined its rules for the 2028 presidential debates, and so far, most announced candidates have met the requirements to participate. Under a new anti-dark money pledge, candidates must explicitly condemn political nonprofits or super PACs that engage in primary election spending, as well as any outside groups that may start supporting them. This move is backed by several elected Democrats, including Senators Elizabeth Warren and Andy Kim, along with Vermont Independent Senator Bernie Sanders. The rules also stipulate that candidates cannot enter into joint fundraising agreements with local party organizations unless they are officially nominated, designed to maintain the Democratic Party's neutrality across different levels. articles.title: Tech Industry Faced with Growing Sense of Hostility Towards Programmers
articles.summary: A growing sense of unease has settled over the world's tech industry, as programmers begin to feel increasingly unwelcome in their own field.
articles.content: A growing sense of unease has settled over the world's tech industry, as programmers begin to feel increasingly unwelcome in their own field. Chemistry and computer science are not so different, a former programmer reflects on their own experiences. In the years following Facebook's IPO, US computer science departments were flooded with students who would have otherwise pursued careers on Wall Street - and it was this influx that sparked widespread resentment among some segments of society. The hostility towards technology is not necessarily driven by opposition to technological advancements themselves, but rather a distaste for the people who create them - the programmers. Many Americans view these upstarts as outsiders, untrustworthy and lacking in traditional values, which has led to a growing distrust of the tech industry and its practitioners. A public math education in Korea had provided this individual with a solid foundation in computer science, making their entry into the field relatively smooth. The discovery of Haskell led to a significant shift in my understanding of computer science and programming languages. Rewriting a code base using a library inspired by Haskell concepts allowed me to grasp its intricacies better. My initial impression of Haskell as a difficult language tied to category theory proved to be true, but the challenge was also what made it appealing. Interacting with researchers in the field of programming languages, known as PL, provided valuable insights into their work and passion for the subject. These researchers are akin to poets, pouring over intricate code and theoretical concepts with a level of dedication that's rare in computer science. Their focus on creating and understanding programming languages is driven by an intrinsic desire to innovate, rather than external pressures like profit margins. This uncommercial nature lends a sense of dignity to their work, setting it apart from other areas of computer science. The influence of Haskell soon spilled over into my personal projects outside of work, as I found myself experimenting with programming in my free time. As a programmer, I had grown accustomed to taking on projects that allowed me to experiment with new languages and tools. This was often done without much regard for the project's overall impact or feasibility, as long as it provided an opportunity to learn something new. My approach to work was not exactly conventional, but it suited my needs at the time. I volunteered to switch teams and took on projects that aligned with my personal interests in programming languages. During company hackathons, I would often create domain-specific languages that catered to specific needs or tasks. These mini-projects allowed me to explore new concepts and ideas without being bogged down by more complex requirements. My online presence was modest but noticeable, with a few contributions to the official TypeScript compiler and some gold badges on Stack Overflow. While not particularly exceptional, these achievements reflected my dedication to learning and improving my skills. As I continued to work in the field, I began to notice a shift in the industry's dynamics. The arrival of ChatGPT in 2022 marked a significant turning point, with its ability to generate code using neural networks sparking both excitement and concern among programmers. While not entirely new, the concept of using neural networks for code generation had gained momentum in recent years. Andrej Karpathy's blog featured an early example of this technology in 2015, where an LSTM was used to create plausible-looking C code. The rise of coding tools has sparked a mix of emotions among programmers. Some see them as a welcome aid, while others feel threatened by their potential to replace human skills. The effectiveness of these tools is undeniable, but it's essential to acknowledge the limitations that come with relying on them. The question remains: would you choose to pair-program with a competent colleague or rely on coding tools? Even if your partner were an exceptional programmer like Linus Torvalds, the answer might still lean towards using LLMs. They offer a certain level of convenience and efficiency, allowing you to focus on higher-level tasks. However, relying on AI can have unintended consequences. As one writer who has experienced this firsthand notes, their ability to code has declined significantly since they began relying more heavily on coding tools. This is not just about writing sentences, but also about losing the finer senses that writers need to protect. The term "programmer may soon become outdated. With AI handling the bulk of the programming tasks, humans are relegated to a supporting role, prompting and guiding the agents that do the actual work. This shift in dynamics raises questions about the nature of the profession and what it means to be a programmer. In essence, programmers have transitioned from being skilled craftsmen to becoming operators or managers of AI systems. It's as if cooks had stopped preparing meals themselves and now only write recipes for others to follow. This change is not just about the tasks involved but also about the level of expertise required. The impact of this shift on the industry is still unclear, but it's undeniable that the role of programmers has evolved significantly. The emphasis has moved from writing code to overseeing and fine-tuning AI systems. This transformation has sparked a range of reactions, from excitement over the potential for increased productivity to concerns about job security and the future of human skills. The debate surrounding coding tools and their impact on the programming profession is complex and multifaceted. While they offer convenience and efficiency, they also raise questions about the value of human expertise and the long-term consequences of relying too heavily on AI. The rise of AI-powered coding tools has led to a significant shift in the way programming is done. What was once a complex and nuanced craft is now being handled by machines, leaving human programmers behind. This change has been gradual, with each new innovation building on previous ones. From bytes to assembly languages, we've developed higher-level tools that simplify the process of writing code. But with AI, we've reached a new level of abstraction, one where humans are no longer needed for tasks that were once their domain. The result is a loss of control and a diminished sense of accomplishment. Some might argue that this is just another step in the evolution of programming. After all, each new advancement has made the process easier and more efficient. But as we cede control to machines, something essential to the craft is lost. Programming is no longer about problem-solving or creative expression, but rather about executing pre-programmed instructions. The impact on individual programmers is also significant. Gone are the days of working on complex projects that require deep concentration and attention to detail. Instead, tasks are now automated, leaving humans with a shallow sense of engagement. This can be seen in the way people interact with AI-powered coding tools like Claude Code. One user spent 10 hours in Claude Code without realizing it, only to discover their usage later. This led them to write a program to block themselves from using the tool except for two days a week. However, they soon found themselves trying to undo this restriction, highlighting the addictive nature of these AI-powered tools. The machine zone" that cultural anthropologist Natasha Dow Schüll described in her book Addiction by Design is eerily similar to what's happening with programming today. People become so engrossed in using AI-powered coding tools that they lose track of time and their surroundings. This can have serious consequences, both for individuals and society as a whole. The loss of human expertise and the long-term consequences of relying too heavily on AI are just two of the many questions being raised by this shift. As we continue down this path, it's essential to consider the impact on our skills, our creativity, and our very way of life. The ability to program has become increasingly accessible, but this convenience comes at a cost: our interest in learning new languages has waned significantly. To build an iOS meditation timer app, I had initially wanted to learn Swift, Apple's programming language for iPhone and Mac apps, but that goal is now unattainable due to the machine's ability to perform tasks with minimal human involvement. I've already built a dozen iOS and Mac apps without knowing anything about Swift syntax, including a version of SelfControl, an internet blocker, which I created by leveraging the machine's capabilities. The machine also developed a new clipboard manager that ensured auditable security. The experience has left me questioning my career as a programmer, and I suspect that in the future, I will continue to dabble with code but no longer pursue it professionally. This realization came after I decided to quit my job to focus on writing a book I had been working on. As a programmer, I've gained insight into the industry's inner workings, including the process of obtaining a green card through an employer, which has become increasingly common in this field. However, I'm not sorry to leave this profession behind as it becomes more dominated by machines. The loss of polyglot programming skills and the ability to appreciate the complexities of multiple languages will be a significant blow to human creativity and innovation as we cede control to machines. articles.title: UN Climate Talks Collapse Amid Fossil Fuel Disagreements
articles.summary: Pacific island nations have expressed deep despair over the collapse of UN climate talks in Turkey, citing a collective failure to address the climate crisis. The small nations are among those most vulnerable to rising sea levels caused by global warming.
articles.content: Pacific island nations have expressed deep despair over the collapse of UN climate talks in Turkey, citing a collective failure to address the climate crisis. The small nations are among those most vulnerable to rising sea levels caused by global warming. The finger of blame is being pointed at various countries, with some opposition politicians in Australia calling for the resignation of Energy Minister Chris Bowen, who led the negotiations as president of COP31. However, it appears that the real issue lies in the inability of countries to work together. A final agreement was rejected due to pressure from oil-producing nations like Saudi Arabia, which opposed any mention of fossil fuels' role in global warming. This lack of a collective approach has resulted in the collapse of the talks for the first time since Copenhagen in 2009. The failure comes at a critical juncture, as the UN's environmental body has confirmed that global temperatures are set to exceed the 1.5°C threshold, leading to more extreme weather events. This lack of collective action is causing a sense of desperation among nations most vulnerable to climate change impacts. The Australian government's handling of the COP31 talks has come under fire from opposition leaders, who are calling for a change in leadership. Angus Taylor, a right-wing member of the Australian parliament, has been vocal in his criticism of Chris Bowen, the country's climate minister. In a scathing assessment, Taylor described Bowen as "a complete and utter failure" when it comes to addressing the nation's climate commitments. Bowen, however, shifted the blame for the summit's lack of progress onto other countries' strong stance on climate change. He pointed out that many nations had drawn red lines around their demands, making it difficult to reach a unified agreement. The climate minister also acknowledged that the talks took place in a highly charged geopolitical environment, with soaring energy prices and the ongoing fallout from the Middle East war adding to the pressure for unity. As countries struggled to find common ground on fossil fuels, Bowen's plan to secure an overarching "cover decision began to unravel. Australia's opposition members expressed outrage over the country's handling of COP31, questioning Prime Minister Anthony Albanese about his decision-making process in the parliament. Albanese faced scrutiny for not taking firmer action against Environment Minister Bowen, who had been leading Australia's climate negotiations at the conference, despite the country investing heavily in it. The opposition members pointed out that A$150 million ($99.23 million) had been spent on COP31 with little to show for it. Albanese did not directly address whether he would ask Bowen to step down, but reiterated his government's commitment to addressing climate change. He emphasized the importance of Australia acting in its national interest, stating Whether it's environmental security or national security, we act in Australia's national interest. The UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres shared the frustration and disappointment of those who had expected more from COP31. In a statement, he expressed his deep dismay at the lack of progress made during the conference. The record overtime session on Sunday highlighted the failure to reach a final agreement, despite the presence of over 190 countries and more than 92,000 registered participants, making it provisionally the largest UN climate conference on record. The international community has been left reeling after the failure to reach a final agreement at COP31, and Pacific island nations are among those expressing their deep disappointment. Foreign ministry spokesman Guo Jiakun emphasized that addressing climate change is a collective responsibility, stating it's a shared undertaking for humanity that cannot be ignored. He also highlighted the irreversible shift towards low-carbon development globally. Pacific island nations, particularly vulnerable to rising sea levels and other climate-related threats, have been left feeling let down by the lack of progress at COP31. The Marshall Islands delegation issued a statement expressing their deep disappointment with the outcome. Tuvalu's climate minister, Maina Talia, expressed concern about the lack of commitment to put the world back on track for the global temperature goal, stating listening to parties who diminish the credibility of signs of climate change is disappointing". articles.title: Elon Musk's Foundation Donates $400 Million in 2025
articles.summary: The Musk Foundation donated nearly $400 million in 2025, a significant decrease from the previous year.
articles.content: Elon Musk's philanthropic efforts have been met with scrutiny, with his foundation's latest tax filing revealing that nearly $400 million was donated in 2025. However, it appears that most of this giving went to another nonprofit founded by Musk. The total donation is a significant decrease from the record-breaking $474 million given out in 2024. Meanwhile, the foundation's assets have seen substantial growth, increasing by over $1 billion to approximately $16 billion. This boost was largely driven by a substantial gift of Tesla shares valued at $64 million. The disparity between the foundation's assets and its donations has raised concerns about its compliance with tax regulations. Private foundations are generally required to distribute around 5% of their investment assets each year, or face excise taxes from the IRS. The Musk Foundation has previously fallen short of this minimum, according to a report by Forbes. The foundation operates with minimal staff, listing only three directors: Elon Musk himself, his family-office head Jared Birchall, and Matilda Simon. In addition, Musk is also listed as president and reportedly dedicates just one hour per week to the organization's activities. The Foundation's allocation of funds reveals a significant portion is directed towards The Foundation itself, a nonprofit established by Musk to oversee a STEM-focused school in Bastrop, Texas. This educational endeavor aims to expand its offerings beyond primary and secondary levels, with plans to eventually establish a university. A substantial $20 million was also channeled into a donor-advised fund at Fidelity Charitable, where Musk retains advisory influence. Donors contributing to these funds can claim tax deductions upfront, while later recommending grants to chosen charities. It's worth noting that once the money is deposited, the sponsoring organization takes control of the funds, with the donor retaining advisory privileges. Critics have previously raised concerns about the structure of these funds, questioning whether they allow donors like Musk to minimize their tax liabilities without promptly distributing resources to active charities. This issue was highlighted in a 2022 report by philanthropy experts who expressed similar reservations about the effectiveness of such arrangements. Funds were also allocated to several Memphis-based organizations, which have ties to xAI and its Colossus data centers. Specifically, Slingshot Memphis received $5.9 million for its efforts to assess the efficacy of poverty-reduction programs using data-driven research and evaluations. Regional One Health Foundation was granted $9.4 million to support patient care initiatives within their organization. Elon Musk's philanthropic efforts have been a subject of interest in recent years, particularly given his commitment to giving away the majority of his wealth during his lifetime or through his will. According to estimates, Musk has given around $1.4 billion from 2021 to 2024, despite his net worth growing by hundreds of billions of dollars over the same period. This is a notable achievement, especially considering that most of his wealth remains tied up in shares of SpaceX and Tesla. The foundation's 2025 giving, amounting to around 0.05% of Musk's estimated $812 billion net worth, underscores the disparity between his philanthropic efforts and his overall wealth.
